findings.span: Buy any 2 Minimalist products, get a FREEBIE of your choice!
findings.why: The mechanic described next is a coupon (B2G3RDFREE) that makes the lowest-priced of three cart items free, not a freebie of the shopper's choice for buying two. The headline makes the same promise, so the offer is misstated.
findings.fix: Add any 3 Minimalist products to your cart and use coupon B2G3RDFREE to get the lowest priced item free.

findings.why: 'Science-backed' is an evidence claim; as broad brand positioning a reviewer may accept it, but it needs a basis the brand can point to.
findings.fix: Keep it if the brand's substantiation basis is on file; otherwise use 'Minimalist skincare that fits your budget.'

tone_read: Mostly plain and practical, which suits an offer ad; the all-caps 'FREEBIE' and exclamation mark add a little promo energy. No fear or agitation.
language_read: No active or concentration is named, which is acceptable for a pure offer creative. The main language problem is that the headline and first line describe a different offer from the coupon mechanic, while the image ('Three products, At the cost of two') matches the coupon.
